summary: Natalie Gummer works in Buddhist and religious studies. She held a post at Harvard University (attested 2001) and became professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Stephan Beyer, and also studied under Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lekden, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.
Natalie Rothman is a historian who studied at the University of Michigan from 1999 to 2006. In 2006, she took up a post at the University of Toronto.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from Harvard in 2005. She was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley (attested 2008) and an assistant professor at UCLA (attested 2016).

Natasha Reichle completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley, supervised by Joanna Gottfried Williams. Working in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, she also studied under Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.
Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen between circa 2012 and 2018 under the supervision of Hans T. Bakker.

Nathan Sivin was a Sinologist and historian of science who studied at the Defense Language Institute, MIT, and Harvard. He held posts at MIT, served as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (circa 1977–2006), and was honorary professor at the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Nathan W. Hill is a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at Harvard under Leonard van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff. He served as reader at SOAS University of London (circa 2008–2019) and held a post at Trinity College Dublin in 2021.
Nathaniel Brassey Halhed was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Harrow School, he worked as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.

Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and also studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Namdrol.

Nathmal Tatia was an Indologist and philosopher. He earned a Doctor of Literature at the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee, also studying under Sukhlal Sanghvi, and served as director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (attested 1982–1990).
Navina Lamminger is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Nawang Tsering Shakspo is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who completed his doctoral studies under Lal Mani Joshi. He served as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).
Neal Arvid Donner is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of British Columbia, where his teachers included Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).
Ng-Fung Yuen specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of the West under the supervision of Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya (attested 2009).
Ngan-che Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Jing Yin (attested 2007) and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.
Ngawang Jinpa was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery. He served as a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling (attested 1995).
Ngawang Jorden is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.

Ngawang Samten works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers including Lati Rinpoche, served as director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held appointments at Smith College, Hampshire, Amherst College, and the University of Tasmania.
Nguyen Thi Tuyet is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Punjabi University under Inder Mohan Singh (attested 2012), while also studying under traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.
